key_insight: PINNs miss shocks in steady inviscid airfoil flows because the steady Euler residuals are too weak to overcome neural networks’ smooth-function bias, so the model gets stuck in a smooth local minimum.
engineering_relevance: This work offers a more reliable physics-informed route for high-speed aerodynamic simulation, especially for capturing shock structures in inviscid airfoil flows without relying on traditional CFD-only solvers.
method: Reformulate steady shock capturing as an unsteady relaxation process toward the steady state.
Use unsteady Euler equations with time-derivative terms to strengthen the physics loss and guide shock formation.
Embed pseudo time-stepping in the PDE loss and simplify the Euler formulation to improve shock-capture accuracy.
evidence_signal: The method was validated on four forward problems with different flow conditions and geometries, showing improved shock-capturing performance in the abstract.
watch_item: Because the approach introduces pseudo-time evolution and long-horizon unsteady constraints, training stability and scalability may still be challenging for harder 3D or high-Mach cases.
paper_title: Physics-informed neural networks for shock capturing in inviscid flows around an airfoil
